title: Citation Chaining Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: A vis-network citation graph of eight illustrative papers in which an arrow from X to Y means X cites Y. The learner answers five citation-chaining questions in a fixed order, one attempt each, by selecting the set of papers found by backward chaining, forward chaining, or a combination of the two from the seed paper S. After each answer the sim highlights the edges followed and explains why; the final score is reported as n of 5 correct with a mastery threshold of 4.

learningObjectives: Solve five citation-chaining questions on a graph of eight papers by following references backward and citations forward, with at least 4 of 5 correct
Recognize that forward chaining reaches newer papers and backward chaining reaches older ones
prerequisites: the meaning of a citation edge

accessibility.notes: The graph has an aria-label that lists every paper, year, and citation edge, and every paper has a keyboard-reachable details button. Answers are native checkboxes; Enter on a checkbox submits. Edge direction is shown with arrowheads, followed edges are drawn thick, correct papers carry a check-mark glyph, wrong picks an X glyph and a dashed border, and feedback is in words; colors are from the Okabe-Ito blue/orange palette. Mouse-wheel zoom and drag-to-pan are disabled so the iframe never captures page scrolling; navigation buttons are provided.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Procedure practice on a concrete graph with one attempt per question, immediate reveal of the correct set, highlighted edges, and a one-sentence reason
keyQuestions: Which papers does this procedure find?
Which papers are found by backward chaining one step from S?
Which papers are found by forward chaining one step from S?
commonMisconceptions: Forward and backward chaining find the same papers
Only papers with matching keywords are relevant
The most recent paper is the most foundational
assessmentOpportunities: At least 4 of 5 questions correct on the first attempt, with each selected set equal to the answer set exactly
Dragging nodes and reading paper details is exploration and is not evidence

controls.name: Paper details
controls.purpose: Show the year, role, references, and citing papers of S, A, B, C, D, E, F, or G (exploration, not scored)

controls.name: Answer papers
controls.purpose: Select the papers A to G that answer the current question; the seed paper S is never part of an answer

controls.name: Submit answer
controls.purpose: Lock the selected set for the current question and show feedback; one attempt per question

controls.name: Next question
controls.purpose: Advance to the next question in the fixed order after the current question has been answered
